title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 145
paragraphs: These were the oracles that had been given to the Athenians. When those Greeks who had the better mind about Greece met together in one place, considered their affairs and exchanged assurances with one another, they decided that their first step of all should be to reconcile their mutual enmities and bring to an end the wars they were currently waging against one another. Other states had wars on their hands, but especially the Athenians had one with the Aeginetans. After this, having been informed that Xerxes was at Sardis with his army, they resolved to send spies to Asia to observe the king's strength, and to send envoys to Argos to make an alliance against the Persian, and others to Sicily to Gelon son of Dinomenes, and others to Corcyra, urging them to come to the help of Greece, and others again to Crete — with the aim that if possible the Greek race might unite as one and that all might act together toward the same end, since dangers threatened all Greeks equally. Gelon's power was said to be great, far greater than any other Greek state's.
